column1: {"narrative": "I have received text messages and phone calls from XXXX Harris & Harris for over two years. They say in the texts it is for debt collection for XXXX XXXX ( {\u00245700.00} ) over XXXX XXXX XXXX. No messages are ever left on my voice mail. I dont even know where this is, nor have I to my knowledge ever crossed this tunnel. The texts are brief and include a link to click on, but I have not clicked on this link for fear of stealing my data. I have never received anything in writing. There is also a direction to enter STOP if I want to be removed from the texts, but that also makes me nervous so I have just ignored them."}

{"narrative": "Long ago in the middle of pandemic I was told that they offered services to help with payments such as delayed payments, haunt on interest rates etc. I called to try and have this done and was told no we do not even tho it stated on their app they did, was also told they would not stop the frequency of calls. Eventually I started catching up with bills after finding work and childcare in the pandemic but it barely covered interest rates. I tried again with no evail my payments weren't enough and they wanted more and more n I told them that was impossible unless me and my kids stopped eating and paying bills. I was talked over everytime, most times by someone XXXX XXXX and ignored untill I hung up. The calls have become more frequent. 2 sometimes 3 times a day. This is way to much and I have had enough!"}

{"narrative": "Portfolio Recoveries has been contacting me repeatedly on both my cell phone numbers as well as my home phone number daily, for over a year regarding an aged debt. After verifying the original date of delinquency from an older credit report, I then compared it to a more current XXXX and saw that the debt had been re-aged. I immediately disputed the validity of the debt with the credit bureaus who moved the account earlier in 2015. The calls had stopped temporarily, then started again and it began relentless. I even told the person the debt was aged and they continued to call. At XXXX point, I said that debt was no longer mine with the though process that since the debt was no longer collectible, that would be the correct tactic. To no avail, the calls will not stop."}
